instruction: Navigate to slide 2 and set its title to "E-Commerce Platform", using the same red color as the first slide's title.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Variation changes the title text from 'Online Shopping' to 'E-Commerce Platform' while keeping the same red color (#FF0000) from slide 1. Verified: slide 1 has title 'Sustainable Energy' in red RGB(255,0,0).
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for correct title text, 0.5 for correct color, 1.0 for both correct

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Getter logic flaw - returns first non-empty text shape instead of specifically extracting the title shape
The getter iterates through all shapes and returns the first one with text, not necessarily the title placeholder
PowerPoint slides have multiple text shapes (title, subtitle, body), and iteration order is unreliable for identifying titles
This will cause false negatives (correct title present but getter reads wrong shape) or false positives (wrong shape has expected text)
Color extraction returns None if color is theme-based or not explicitly set, which won't match expected [255, 0, 0]
Expected values appear semantically correct (text='E-Commerce Platform', color=RGB(255,0,0))
Postconfig is appropriate (activates window, saves file with Ctrl+S)
Metric comparison logic is correct with proper partial credit (0.5 for text, 0.5 for color)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Use shape.is_placeholder and shape.placeholder_format.type to identify title placeholder specifically
Or use slide.shapes.title property if available in python-pptx library
Add proper title shape identification logic: check for PP_PLACEHOLDER.TITLE type
Handle theme-based colors more robustly - convert theme colors to RGB or handle None case
Add validation that the extracted shape is actually a title, not just any text shape
